free_tier.stated: No free tier on this plan. Mikrus 1.0 is PLN 35 a year gross, printed '35 zł / rok (brutto)'. The vendor also runs a separate free product, FROG, at 256 MB and 3 GB, which requires a one-off deposit of at least PLN 5 as identity verification and is restricted to users in Poland.

retention.stated: annual prepay; the terms allow withdrawal within 14 days if the delivered server does not match the advertised resources. The separate free FROG service deletes servers nobody has logged into for 3 months.

egress.terms: no byte allowance published on the plan card; the vendor's IPv6 article states 'Nie limitujemy, ile portów zużyjesz na adresacji prywatnej oraz ile wykorzystasz na adresacji IPv6' (we do not limit how much you use on private addressing or on IPv6 addressing)

interface_detail: LXC container with full root, in Finland, managed entirely over SSH; a panel at ssp.mikr.us handles restart, reinstall and password changes
tooling: any SSH client; the vendor's panel; free subdomains and automatic HTTPS for web services
chaining: a 384 MB container at USD 0.7429 a month whose three forwarded ports include two that carry both TCP and UDP, in a Polish-language product built around IPv6-mostly addressing

limits.value: 3 forwarded ports on the shared IPv4: SSH at 10000 plus the account ID, and two free ports at 20000 and 30000 plus the ID, which can be extended with 5 more TCP ports in the panel for a total of 7
no byte allowance published; the IPv6 article states the only real limit is RAM

binding_note: three forwarded ports, only two of which are freely usable, is a smaller inbound budget than any other in-stock row, and the two free ports carry both protocols so one of them goes to WireGuard.

identity_cost.detail: the order form requires a real first name, last name and email address: the terms state 'Podczas składania zamówienia niezbędne jest podanie prawdziwego imienia, nazwiska oraz adresu e-mail'. Payment is by Polish bank transfer through the TPAY processor (Krajowy Integrator Płatności S.A.), which passes the buyer's address data back to the vendor, so a bank account is the instrument rather than a card. VAT invoices are issued on request to a company or a private individual. No national ID number is requested.

reliability_note: the vendor states its servers run in 'głównie IPv6' (mostly IPv6) mode rather than IPv6-only, and publishes an article explaining the trade-off; no uptime figure or SLA published
confidence_note: price, shape, location, the VAT invoice option and the order-field requirement are quoted from the vendor's own order page and terms read today; the port scheme, the dual TCP/UDP capability and the IPv6-mostly design are quoted from the vendor's own wiki article read today; the VAT ID is quoted from the vendor's own site metadata. The cart was not exercised, so the payment step is documented from the terms rather than observed.

notes: The only row that is genuinely built around IPv6 by design rather than as a way to avoid buying IPv4: the vendor publishes an article explaining that its servers run in 'głównie IPv6' mode, not IPv6-only, and that it deliberately keeps IPv4 scarce so it does not have to buy addresses at about USD 57 each. That is a first-party account of the economics, in Polish, and it is the kind of thing an English search does not surface. The port story is better than the headline suggests and worse than the best rows here: three ports to start, of which two are freely usable, and both of those carry TCP and UDP - the vendor names OpenVPN and WireGuard explicitly - with five more TCP ports free from the panel for a ceiling of seven. At PLN 35 a year gross, which is USD 8.915 a year or USD 0.7429 a month at 3.9261 PLN per USD read today, 384 MB and 5 GB NVMe in Finland is good value. Two things hold it to a caveat. The identity story is a bank transfer through a Polish payment processor that passes the buyer's address back to the vendor, and the terms require a real first name and surname, so this is not an email-only signup; a foreign buyer without a Polish bank account has no published route. And no traffic allowance is published anywhere, which is a documented absence rather than a limit and cannot be used in arithmetic. The VAT ID PL6821639338 is printed in the site metadata and the vendor states it issues VAT invoices, which is more entity disclosure than most rows, though the trading company name behind the VAT number was not read. The separate free FROG product is Poland-only and requires a PLN 5 identity deposit, so it is not available for a user. What is not established: the payment step, since the cart was not exercised, and whether a non-Polish bank transfer is accepted.
